contents:
Hi, I&rsquo;m Your Name. This is my personal website, built with Hugo and the Kana theme.
I use this site to write longer posts, keep short notes, and track the books I read. There&rsquo;s no comment section and no tracking — just words on a page.
What I write about Software engineering and tooling Books I&rsquo;m reading or have finished Whatever is on my mind at the moment If you&rsquo;d like to get in touch, the best way is email. You can also subscribe to the RSS feed to follow along.

Privacy This site is a static website. It does not run any analytics, advertising, or tracking scripts, and it does not set cookies. There is nothing to collect because nothing is collected.
Comments There is no comment system. If you want to respond to something you read here, email me or reply from your own blog — I love a good web-ring.
Affiliate links Some book links in the library may point to bookstores. They are there for convenience, not commission.

contents:
The Kana theme does not change how you write Markdown, but it does add a few helpful extras. Here are the ones I use most.
Syntax highlighting with a filename Add a file attribute to a fenced code block and the theme will label it:
main.gopackage main import &#34;fmt&#34; func main() { fmt.Println(&#34;Hello from a Hugo code block&#34;) }The highlighting uses the Gruvbox palette.
Collapsible code blocks Long snippets can be folded away with details=true:
Detailshugo new content …
title: Code Blocks, Captions, and Other Hugo Tricks

contents:
I write to think. There is something about putting a half-formed idea into sentences that forces me to notice where the idea is actually hollow.
Writing as a filter When a thought stays in my head, it feels complete. The moment I try to write it down, the gaps show up. Writing is how I separate the ideas that survive contact with a keyboard from the ones that only sounded good at 2 a.m.
